title: EOS — raise bounded Claude turn ceiling for correction jobs
intent:
Correct the hard EOS Claude runtime ceiling that caused both #836 and #837 to terminate at exactly 40 turns before completing otherwise bounded correction work.

Required work:
Make the Claude max-turn limit an explicit bounded runtime policy instead of a fixed 40-turn ceiling that is too small for governed correction jobs.

Requirements:
- Preserve `dontAsk`; do not enable `bypassPermissions` or unrestricted Bash.
- Preserve all existing tool allowlists, cost/capacity semantics, routing, verifier, integration, and provider boundaries.
- Keep a finite ceiling; do not make turns unlimited.
- Set a safer bounded default for EOS correction/implementation work of 80 turns, or implement a task-class policy where ordinary analysis remains <=40 and bounded correction/implementation may use <=80.
- Record the configured turn ceiling in runtime telemetry/status so future failures are diagnosable.
- A max-turn termination must remain FAILED/BLOCKED rather than COMPLETE.
- Add focused regressions proving a task that requires >40 but <=80 turns is not terminated by the old ceiling, while >configured-limit execution still fails closed.
- Do not attempt to solve #834/#835 completion semantics in this issue.

Completion:
Produce a governed patch/result or draft PR containing only the bounded turn-policy correction and tests. Report exact changed files, old/new ceiling behavior, tests, and whether safe to merge. Do not merge automatically.
scope: Inspect only the Claude wake/runtime configuration path that constructs the `claude -p` invocation, starting with the existing wake supervisor/runtime module and its focused tests. Do not inspect Taylor product code, Agent Manager, Cortex provider logic, project-keystone, or unrelated workflows.
